svg.title: Titration curve of a diprotic acid
svg.desc: pH against volume of strong base for a diprotic weak acid. The curve rises through a first buffer region, passes through pH equal to pKa1, 4.0, at half the first equivalence volume, climbs steeply at the first equivalence point at 25 millilitres, rises through a second buffer region where pH equals pKa2, 9.0, at the point halfway to the second equivalence point, and climbs steeply again at the second equivalence point at 50 millilitres. Two equivalence points mean two acidic protons. The major species changes from H2A to HA minus to A two minus along the curve. Illustrative data.
svg.text: Two protons, two equivalence points, two pKa values
Each acidic proton gives its own equivalence point: two equivalence points mean two acidic protons.
